title: Clever Hans: the horse that read faces
summary: A horse seemed to do arithmetic. A student found he was reading cues from the questioner. Researchers use the same label for models that are right for the wrong reason.

beats.say: A horse seemed to do arithmetic. He was reading the humans.
His trainer, Wilhelm von Osten, asked questions. Hans answered by tapping a hoof.
In nineteen oh four, a panel of thirteen found no trick.
Then a student, Oskar Pfungst, ran controlled tests.
With the questioner in view, Hans got fifty of fifty six right.
With his view blocked, he got two of thirty five.
The questioner tensed as taps neared the answer, then relaxed at the last tap.
Hans was never counting. He was reading when to stop.
Researchers use the same label for models that are right for the wrong reason.
beats.cap: The Clever Hans effect, in AI

claims.note: Wikipedia, Clever Hans: the 1904 commission led by Carl Stumpf had 13 members
Wikipedia, Clever Hans: with the questioner visible Hans was right 50 of 56 times (89%)
Wikipedia, Clever Hans: with the questioner not visible Hans was right 2 of 35 times (6%)

facts.claim: Wilhelm von Osten trained Hans in Berlin, and Hans appeared to answer questions with hoof taps
facts.note: Britannica, Clever Hans: trainer Wilhelm von Osten; Berlin; exhibitions from 1891; answered by hoof taps

facts.claim: A 13-member panel led by Carl Stumpf concluded in September 1904 that no tricks were involved
facts.note: Wikipedia, Clever Hans: 13-member commission, September 1904, no tricks

facts.claim: Oskar Pfungst published a report in 1907 finding Hans responded to subtle, probably involuntary cues from the questioner
facts.note: Britannica: Pfungst, student at the Psychological Institute, University of Berlin; report 1907; 'very subtle, probably involuntary, cues'

facts.claim: Hans got 50 of 56 right when he could see the questioner and 2 of 35 when he could not
facts.note: Wikipedia, Clever Hans: Pfungst's blinder tests; visible 50 of 56 (89%); not visible 2 of 35 (6%)

facts.claim: The questioner's posture and expression tensed as the taps approached the right answer and relaxed at the last tap
facts.note: Wikipedia, Clever Hans: cause of the effect

facts.claim: The term Clever Hans effect is also used for AI models that appear to predict correctly for the wrong reasons
facts.note: Wikipedia, Clever Hans, Machine learning / AI section
